item.title: Re: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
The idea of the organic Dyson sphere is a really interesting one, but the idea the organism is getting energy from a star, something extremely hot, but grows faster in extreme cold seems a bit contradictory.

Maybe have the Dyson sphere primarily powering the portal and potentially the organism have some form of organic superconductor properties which allow for better energy extraction in the lower temperature?

I’m just spitballing though, definitely interested in an organic Dyson sphere.

item.title: Re: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
Oh my… I just typed out a massive, comprehensive response, but wikidot said, "Would be a shame if something happened to it." Here's the cliff notes version:

Location: The temperature (cold=entity grow big fast, hot=entity grow big slower) is a main factor - cold helps smaller entities grow quickly, and solar/thermal energy sustains large entities. The coordinates are just random, but added for authenticity. The portal, admittedly, is more for narrative purposes than anything else - I'll tie it in somehow.

Neutralization: The core of the biomass (the maw and star) is essentially an organic Dyson Sphere. At times, though, it draws hydrogen aggressively from the star, but always at a sustainable rate. The final MTF squad discover something terrible enough that it convinces them to destroy the system with extreme prejudice. In a stroke of genius, one of the members destroys a section of a cortex just below the Maw that controls inhibitions, thus causing the Maw to begin extracting huge quantities of hydrogen. This sends the star into an implosion, and however durable the biomass may be, it cannot survive a dying star. That also destroys the pair of portals—the damage inflicted to the one within the system corresponds to the one on earth.

I know that there's still a bunch of refining to do, and rest assured, I intend to do it. Thanks again for your response!

item.title: Re: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
I think you've got an interesting concept on your hands, but I do feel like it could do with some refining.

+ Spoilers
- Spoilers

Like why exactly is the crash site specifically within 2km of 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E? Was it just luck that it wasn't in a more populated area? The size of the entity and the amount of biomass at it's disposal makes it seem slightly silly that its only a specific and small crash site without justified reasoning.

The portal seems a bit too 'Avengers 1' with an explosion through a portal into outer space, instantly neutralizing all elements of the skip. It feels like a obvious weak point of the entity that clearly has some form of higher or complex intelligence.

I do look forward to seeing the finished result and I do really like the mix of bodysnatchers, Lovecraft and The Thing going on!

item.title: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
I understand that new authors typically don't write Keter-class scips, but this one just stuck with me, so here I am.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Genre: Mystery, Horror, Action with hints of desperation

Page Layout: Standard format (no ACS)

Elevator Pitch: A solar system that is roughly 2000 Au1 in diameter which is overtaken by a biomass of tremendous proportions. Said biomass is a colonial organism with organic linkages that span the distances between celestial bodies and envelop the planets themselves, effectively turning the entire system into a breeding ground for smaller units of the organism, thus furthering its reach. A central mass which measures ~1.92 million km in diameter engulfs the system's sun, and a large, ovular maw sits atop it.

+Brace Yourself
-You need more time to brace?

[This maw ejects chitinous pods (SCP-XXXX-2) containing small, wormlike entities measuring 45 cm in length (SCP-XXXX-2-A). These pods will crash within a 2 km radius of the coordinates 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E (Antarctica). Approximately one (1) hour after landing, these worms will "hatch" and burrow into the ice. It is shown that organisms proceed to grow at an indeterminate rate while in these conditions.

When exposed to a human being, SCP-XXXX-2-A will merge with the human's spinal column, controlling synapses and effectively taking the subject over. These instances are aggressive to all forms of life and show resistance to pain. Due to this outcome, a mobile task force (Hammer Down, maybe?) will be stationed within this two kilometer zone, and the trajectories of SCP-XXXX-2 will be tracked. Upon finding the crash zone, MTF will destroy SCP-XXXX-2 and SCP-XXXX-2-A by several means (I've written up a list of these means that will be in the official article.)

The final section of this SCP (I promise), referred to as SCP-XXXX-3, is a triangular portal with equa-distant sides that measures 15 meters tall, located at 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E. It transports anyone entering to a corresponding portal within SCP-XXXX-1 (the solar system).
]

SCP-XXXX-1 and SCP-XXXX-3 were destroyed by MTF during an exploration, thus re-classifying SCP-XXXX as neutralized.

Central Narrative: The article contains a few exploration logs, which culminates with an MTF force detonating a large device that cause the star to implode, eviscerating all components of the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Several, the first of which will be the title and the "Keter Neutralized" classification. An image too, if I can find one or make my own.

Additional Notes: I was reading a bit about making first time Scips too complex/long. I fully intend to be as concise as possible (no 1730 here, folks). It might also be a bright idea for the struck-through class to be Keter-alterius, due to its alien origins.

Footnotes
1. [The standard unit of measurement used to delineate extremely large distances]
